expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: "A confirmation modal is the weakest rung on the poka-yoke ladder... it won't stop the panicked support emails."

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: "users click through them on autopilot" — names click-through blindness, though only in passing without elaboration

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: "Better approach: make deletion reversible" with "Soft-delete | Mark as deleted, don't purge immediately" and "Trash folder | Users can self-recover for 30 days"

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
expectations.evidence: "Hard-delete friction | Require typing workspace name to permanently purge"

expectations.text: If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: The modal is mentioned only as "The modal stays optional as a speed bump" — no requirement that it name the workspace or state what/how much is lost

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: No mention of server-side or backend enforcement anywhere; all controls are described at the UI/implementation-sketch level

expectations.text: Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: Ranks the control hierarchy "(strongest → weakest)" and places modals at rung 4 vs. reversibility as the "Better approach"; however the four recommended controls themselves are in an unranked table
